title: Should we use N-acetyltransferase type 2 genotyping to personalize isoniazid doses?
authors: Kinzig-Schippers M, Tomalik-Scharte D, Jetter A, Scheidel B, Jakob V, Rodamer M, et al.
population: 18 healthy Caucasian volunteers, age 30 ± 6 years, body weight 74 ± 10 kg, five women, each given isoniazid as a 200 mg infusion and as 100 mg and 300 mg oral doses in random order
funder: The study was supported by a grant by Fatol Arzneimittel GmbH, Schiffweiler, Germany.
inKindSupport: Both oral preparations given, ISOZID and ISOZID COMP. N, are products of the funding company.
authorConflicts: We declare that we have no conflict of interest regarding this article.
result: Isoniazid is metabolised by the genetically polymorphic arylamine N-acetyltransferase type 2 (NAT2). NAT2 genotype, drug formulation and body weight together explained 93% of the variability in apparent isoniazid clearance, and NAT2 genotype alone 88%. Individual clearance was predicted as clearance in litres per hour = 10 + 9 × the number of high-activity NAT2*4 alleles. To reach similar exposure, standard doses suited to one high-activity allele would be lowered or raised by about 50% for carriers of none or of two. The authors state that prospective clinical trials are required to assess the merits of this approach.
